proposal.blind_spot: The optimizer cannot tell whether these memory-bound kernels are limited by L2 bandwidth, DRAM bandwidth, or global-load latency with unused bandwidth headroom, so it applies the same byte-reduction recipe to all of them and guesses when it fails.

rationale.lts__throughput.avg.pct_of_peak_sustaine: HIGH -> L2 is the real ceiling: reduce sector requests and add on-chip reuse (SMEM tiling for transpose/permute, row caching, vectorization) instead of chasing DRAM bytes / LOW while dram% is HIGH -> DRAM is the true limit: only remove compulsory traffic via fusion and avoiding materialized copies, skip cache-level restructuring
rationale.smsp__warp_issue_stalled_long_scoreboard: HIGH with dram% below peak -> latency-bound: increase memory-level parallelism via more independent loads per thread, unrolling, higher occupancy / LOW with dram% near peak -> bandwidth-saturated: latency-hiding is wasted, only byte elimination helps, and avoid risky rewrites that previously regressed
